how_it_works: One section is pinned to the viewport (GSAP ScrollTrigger `pin: true`, `start: 'top top'`) while the page keeps advancing an internal timeline bound to scroll via `scrub`. The user's scroll becomes the playhead: instead of moving down the page, they scrub forward/back through career 'beats.' Each beat is one role. As scroll progresses, the previous role's title/org/bullets animate out (fade + small y/blur) and the next beat animates in, so the same fixed frame morphs through nference (FT) -> nference (intern) -> AMC clinical -> DEXTER ML -> Animations Media. Concretely: a parent timeline crossfades N beats with `scrub: 0.6-1` (1s catch-up smoothing, not `scrub: true` which jitters on trackpads). Scroll distance controls duration via `end: '+=<px>'`. The hard constraint is the scroll budget: a single pinned scene should stay ~1500px (ceiling ~2000px / roughly 2x viewport height) before users feel trapped, and total pinned scroll across a page should stay under ~6000px (~3x visible content height) or mobile users abandon before the CTA. With 5 career beats that math breaks: 5 beats x ~1200-1500px each = 6000-7500px in ONE pinned block, past the friction ceiling. Practical resolution: either (a) pin only a 2-3 beat 'headline' arc and let the rest scroll normally, or (b) do NOT pin at all — use `scrub` WITHOUT `pin` (element stays in normal document flow, avoids pin-spacer / stacking-context / mobile viewport-resize bugs) and let beats crossfade as the block passes through the viewport. What moves: role title, org name, dates, bullet text, a proof chip, and optionally a large background year. What stays: a persistent section label / progress indicator so fast scrollers always know where they are and can exit.
visual_structure: A single beat is a fixed centered/left-aligned frame: small monospace/label date range (e.g. '2024 — present') top, oversized Fraunces role title (e.g. 'ML Engineer'), Inter org line + location beneath, 2-3 short Inter bullets (each <= 2 lines — 3 lines reads as a paragraph and gets skipped), and one maroon proof chip (metric or stack, e.g. 'clinical NLP · 40% ↓ review time'). A faint oversized ghost year can sit behind for depth (parallax at a slower rate). Beats do not stack in the DOM visually — they occupy the same pinned frame and MORPH: outgoing beat fades to opacity 0 with a ~24-40px upward drift and slight blur, incoming beat fades 0->1 from below, title optionally scaling slightly. A thin fixed progress rail (maroon on paper) or '02 / 05' counter persists across all beats so the frame never feels like a scroll trap. Legibility law: at every scroll position exactly one beat's title + org must be fully readable — never let two titles overlap mid-transition.
motion_recipe: GSAP: `gsap.timeline({ scrollTrigger: { trigger: '.journey', start: 'top top', end: '+=<beats*1200>', pin: true, scrub: 0.8, invalidateOnRefresh: true } })`. Use `scrub: 0.6-1` for a cinematic, jitter-forgiving feel; NEVER `scrub: true` on text-bearing beats (touchpad/wheel ticks show as visible judder). Crossfade beats with opacity + `y` (24-40px) + optional `filter: blur(4px)->0`; title can `scale 1.03->1`. Animate ONLY `transform` + `opacity` (compositor thread; add `force3D: true`); never animate top/left/width/height. Stagger bullets ~0.08-0.12 within a beat. Prevent FOUC with CSS `opacity: 0` + `gsap.fromTo` (not `from`). Initialize inside `document.fonts.ready.then(() => { init(); ScrollTrigger.refresh(); })` because Fraunces/Inter swap shifts trigger positions. Set `ScrollTrigger.config({ ignoreMobileResize: true })`. Show a scroll-progress indicator on the pinned scene. Use `gsap.matchMedia()` — pin+scrub only at `(min-width: 768px)`. Clean up with `useGSAP({ scope })` or `gsap.context()`. What NOT to animate: the pinned trigger element itself (animate its children — animating the trigger breaks pin-spacer math); layout properties; nothing flashing/aggressive-zoom. Do NOT scroll-jack on mobile.
reduced_motion: Under `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)` (and gate all motion behind `no-preference` + `gsap.matchMedia`), drop the pin and the scrub entirely: render every career beat as a normal, statically-stacked vertical list of role cards in native document flow — date, role, org, bullets, proof chip, all visible with zero scroll-linked motion. Substitute, don't just delete: keep a static maroon spine or numbered '01–05' markers so the career sequence/order still reads. Optionally allow instant (non-scrubbed) opacity/color reveals on enter. This static stack is also the correct mobile fallback and, notably, is closer to what a fast-scanning recruiter actually wants — so it doubles as the a11y path and the scannable path.
brand_fit: MEDIUM (leaning LOW if applied to all 5 beats). Reason: A restrained pinned scrub can carry the 'rise-and-dock' hero energy into Experience and feels editorial/cinematic, which suits the Fraunces + maroon-on-paper clinical-AI aesthetic and avoids purple-SaaS slop. BUT the core tension is recruiter friction: hiring managers scan a portfolio in ~3-10s in an F-pattern and treat scroll-jacking, forced sequential reveal, and 'I scrolled forever and nothing happened' as abandonment triggers; 68% screen on mobile where pinned scrubs are the most fragile (pin-spacer + address-bar resize bugs). Pinning ALL 5 beats (nference FT/intern, AMC, DEXTER, Animations Media) forces ~6000-7500px of scroll through one locked frame — over the ~6000px budget and well over the ~2000px single-pin ceiling — meaning a recruiter cannot skim roles in parallel; they must scrub linearly, which is the opposite of a 6-second scan. Verdict: acceptable ONLY if scoped to a short 2-3 beat 'signature' arc with a visible progress indicator and a genuine static fallback, and paired with an always-scannable list; a full 5-beat pinned scrub is a delight-over-utility trap for this audience.
steal: Steal the MORPH, not the pin-length. Keep the beats in normal document flow with `scrub` and NO `pin`, and reuse the same fixed frame layout (date / big Fraunces title / org / bullets / maroon proof chip) so consecutive roles crossfade in place — title fades up + slight blur-to-sharp, bullets stagger — giving 'one continuous journey' polish without ever trapping the scroll. Add a persistent '02 / 05' progress counter so orientation is never lost. This delivers the hero-echo cinematic feel while remaining skimmable and mobile-safe.
avoid: Avoid pinning the entire career and forcing linear scrub through all beats — it creates the classic 'it hijacked my scroll and I felt trapped' / 'I scrolled forever' friction, blows past the ~2000px single-pin and ~6000px total budgets, and is exactly what a time-boxed recruiter penalizes. Concretely: don't disable native scroll, don't hide roles behind sequential scrub with no progress indicator or exit, don't use `scrub: true` on text beats (judder), and never ship the pinned version on mobile. If a recruiter can't see all 5 roles by fast-scrolling or via a static fallback, cut the pin.
live_examples: Apple product pages (e.g. AirPods / iPhone feature scrollytelling) — the canonical pinned-viewport + scroll-scrub storytelling pattern this borrows from, applied to product beats rather than career beats [uncertain: product marketing, not a resume]
